title: After 49 years, Nasa’s Voyager 1 is one light-day away from us. Can we save this ‘pale blue dot’? | Kim Heacox
summary: Since the spacecraft’s 1977 launch, our wonderful and terrible species has done great damage to our planet. Voyager has offered us a clear view of ourselves Imagine traveling nonstop for 49 years, alone in the dark with no destination in sight, powered by curiosity and engineering. Further imagine making that journey not at bullet train or jet plane speed, but much faster: at 37,800 miles per hour, free from friction in a vast sea of cold, soundless space, bombarded by radiation and cosmic rays yet still able to communicate with folks back home. title: Nasa’s Voyager 1 just reached a massive milestone in space - video
summary: Nasa sent the Voyager 1 and 2 probes into space almost 50 years ago to explore the outer reaches of our solar system. Now Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object from Earth, is about to reach a distance of one light-day away from our planet. To find out more about its astonishing journey, Madeleine Finlay hears from Jim Bell, a planetary scientist and professor at Arizona State University’s school of Earth and space exploration. He explains the seismic impact the mission has had on our understanding of the solar system, and where Voyager 1 could be heading now it has left the heliosphere Continue reading...
